context.goal: 新型电力系统断面潮流控制：兼顾时效性、准确性、泛化性与可解释性，在实时运行和极端天气场景强化断面阻塞决策、确保安全裕度并适应电网动态演化。

reference_logic.mechanism: 该假设的逻辑是：边界信息对协同调控的价值随断面安全裕度变化而非恒定；裕度充足时，周期性交换边界电压、联络线功率和支撑区间的边际收益较低，接近约束时新信息更能改变协同动作。因此以预测断面裕度变化和边界功率不一致作为风险信号触发通信，并设置最大静默时间，可在压低消息总量的同时限制关键边界状态的信息龄期和风险检测延迟，从而降低通信负担并控制越限风险。需要区分该收益是否真正来自风险选择性通信，而非单纯降低控制频率或更多启用本地备用。
reference_logic.evidence_needs: 需要独立证据证明：多区域输电断面场景下事件触发消息机制能改善通信量与安全执行的权衡；现有分区、通信网络与分布式优化证据只能说明计算通信耦合和多区域边界协调的必要性，不能直接证明多智能体事件触发策略有效，配电对象结论迁移至输电场景须另行验证。还需通信量、P95全流程时延、边界一致性误差、断面违反率、调节成本、信息龄期和风险检测延迟的配套测量；等消息预算随机触发、固定周期、全通信及单区域控制/分布式优化基线的对照；延迟、丢包和突发丢包下的降级证据；以及通过消融或预算匹配排除“仅降频”或“仅多用备用”解释的证据。
reference_logic.verification: 可在118节点系统划分三个电气区域，在仿真中加入离散事件消息队列和统一时间戳统计；比较全通信、固定周期、等消息预算随机触发和风险触发，并加入单区域控制与分布式优化基线。扫描0%、1%、5%、10%丢包率和跨0至一个控制周期的时延，设置相关突发丢包；统一记录有效消息、超龄回退、计算通信时延和P95时延，检验信息龄期、风险检测延迟与断面违反率的关系。采用同一策略权重减少学习差异，预注册非劣效违反率容差；只有在消息量和通信引起时延下降且违反率在容差内、等预算下风险触发更快发现风险变化时，才支持该机制。持续完全失联仅检验降级能力，不宣称全局最优或绝对安全。
reference_logic.gaps: 待改进包括：触发阈值和最大静默时间缺乏先验整定依据，需做敏感性分析；风险信号定义可能受预测误差影响；等消息预算随机基线的公平性和统计功效需明确；信息龄期的中介效应需因果式检验而非仅相关分析；通信模型可能简化时间同步、协议开销、消息丢失相关性和跨区带宽竞争；失联处置规则与本地备用容量对成本和安全结果的贡献需分离；配电到输电的迁移有效性未验证；非劣效容差和P95时延统计口径需预注册；训练中注入延迟丢包与在线统一潮流校核的一致性需检查；不能从仿真结果外推为绝对安全保证。

context.core_mechanism_constraint: 假设安全裕度充足时边界信息的边际价值较低，而接近约束边界时新信息直接影响协同动作；风险触发将通信集中于高价值时刻，在降低总消息量的同时控制关键状态陈旧性。

hits.file: Seconds-scale renewable AGC security control considering multi-level transmission section constraints
hits.text: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy, fluctuations of non-AGC renewable stations and load disturbances may cause security-boundary violations in multi-level transmission sections. This paper proposes a seconds-scale renewable AGC security-control method that integrates DNN-based fast state estimation, PTDF-based section-to-station sensitivity analysis, and quadratic-programming-based command optimization. The method redistributes AGC commands within a 4-s rolling cycle while coordinating transmission-section security, 15-min dispatch tracking, and renewable energy accommodation. Tests on the IEEE 118-bus system show that the active- and reactive-power relative estimation errors remain below 3% when the measurement-noise level is increased to three times its baseline value. hits.file: Event-Triggered Transmission of Sensor Measurements Using Twin Hybrid Filters for Renewable Energy Resource Management Systems
hits.text: Recently, solar and wind power generation have gained attention as pathways to achieving carbon neutrality, and Renewable Energy Resource Management System (RERMS) technology has been developed to monitor and control small-scale, distributed renewable energy resources. In this work, we present an Event-Triggered Transmission (ETT) algorithm for RERMS, which transmits sensor measurements to the base station only when necessary. The ETT algorithm helps prevent congestion in the communication channel between RERMS and the base station, avoiding time delays or packet loss caused by the excessive transmission of sensor measurements. We design a hybrid state estimation algorithm that combines Kalman and Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters to enhance the estimation performance, and we propose a new ETT algorithm based on this design. hits.file: Event‐triggered communication in wide‐area damping control: a limited output feedback‐based approach
hits.text: A conceptual design methodology is proposed for event‐triggered based communication for wide‐area damping controller in power systems. The event‐triggering mechanism is adopted to reduce the communication burden between the origin of the remote signal and the wide‐area damping controller (WADC) location. The remote signal is transmitted to the WADC only when an event‐triggering condition based on a predefined system output, is satisfied. The triggering condition is derived from a stability criterion, and is monitored continuously by a separate event‐monitoring unit located at the origin of the remote signal. The stability of the resulting closed‐loop system is guaranteed via the input‐to‐state stability technique. The proposed event‐triggered WADC is implemented on two typical test power systems – two area four machine and IEEE 39‐bus 10‐machine. hits.file: Distributed Event-Triggered Voltage Control with Limited Re-Active Power in Low Voltage Distribution Networks
hits.text: A high proportion of photovoltaic (PV) connections to a low-voltage distribution network (LVDN) causes serious voltage problems. In order to ensure voltage stability for renewable energy networks, we propose a distributed reactive voltage control strategy that is event-triggered. The voltage information of the PV nodes is transmitted to the upper layer of the communication network, where the agent calculates the output set value of the PV inverter. The underlying control strategy is based on the voltage sensitivity matrix, and the upper-level control strategy is based on an event-triggered consensus protocol. This strategy can accommodate the requirements for multi-time modeling and control. We verified the convergence of the event-triggered control algorithm using numerical analysis and proved the reduction of the communication times. We conducted case studies and simulation experiments to verify the effectiveness of our proposed voltage control strategies.

hits.file: Event‐triggered distributed optimisation for multi‐agent systems with transmission delay
hits.text: In this study, the authors discuss the event‐triggered distributed optimisation algorithm for multi‐agent systems with sampled‐data and transmission delay. Each agent only knows its local objective function and exchanges information with its connected neighbours through the network. Firstly, they present sufficient conditions of exponential stability for a class of hybrid non‐linear systems by using continuous and discrete analysis. Then, based on these conditions, a distributed optimisation algorithm is proposed such that a multi‐agent system achieves consensus and optimality. Finally, a simulation example is provided to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

hits.file: Resilient Event-Triggered Distributed Economic Dispatch Control Strategy Under DoS Attacks
hits.text: Distributed economic dispatch in AC distribution systems relies heavily on communication networks and is therefore vulnerable to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. To address this issue, this paper proposes a resilient event-triggered distributed economic dispatch control strategy. Two typical DoS attack scenarios, namely communication-link blocking and node isolation, are first modeled, and an event-triggered distributed economic dispatch controller is then developed to maintain incremental cost consensus and system power balance while reducing communication overhead. Based on Lyapunov stability theory and a linear matrix inequality approach, sufficient conditions for the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system are derived, tolerable bounds on the frequency and duration of DoS attacks are established, and the absence of Zeno behavior is proved. hits.file: Design and Implementation of an Energy Management System with Event-Triggered Distributed Secondary Control in DC Microgrids
hits.text: In this paper, an event-triggered distributed secondary control, along with an energy management algorithm, was developed to ensure the voltage stability and power management of a DC microgrid containing batteries and renewable energy sources, such as PV systems and wind turbines. The energy management algorithm, employing fuzzy logic control, governs power flow based on the generation status of sources and the charging rate of the battery. Consequently, the control algorithm shields the battery from overcharging and over-discharging situations, simultaneously ensuring energy quality within the microgrid. Sampled-data-based event-triggered control is integrated into the proposed distributed secondary control to alleviate communication burdens between controllers, effectively avoiding Zeno behavior. hits.file: Resilient Event‐Triggered Load Frequency Control for Interconnected Renewable Power Systems Considering Parameter Uncertainties
hits.text: ABSTRACT Though the integration of renewable energy sources into power grids increases, their inherent intermittency and uncertainty may undermine the effectiveness of conventional load frequency control (LFC) strategies. Distributed LFC (DLFC) has emerged as a promising solution by leveraging distributed control architectures and advanced communication technologies. However, existing DLFC approaches face two major limitations: (1) inaccuracies in small‐signal modelling due to shifts in the system's steady‐state operating point and (2) inefficiencies in conventional event‐triggered control mechanisms, which fail to adapt dynamically to system fluctuations. hits.file: Identification of Critical Security Boundary for Resilient Power Systems Driven by Model‐Data Fusion
hits.text: ABSTRACT With the evolution of power system structure and the expansion of renewable energy scale, the security and stability challenges brought by extreme events are becoming increasingly prominent. hits.text: The high time-variability and multi-dimensional coupling characteristics of distribution and transmission power grids impose severe challenges on conventional reactive power optimization methods, which generally fail to balance real-time response performance and global optimality, thereby easily causing voltage limit violations and excessive network power losses. hits.file: Distributed event-triggered consensus protocols for discrete-time multiagent systems
hits.text: Abstract This paper focuses on leader-following and leaderless consensus problems of discrete-time multiagent systems. A distributed observer-based consensus protocol is proposed to investigate the consensus problem for multiagent systems of general discrete-time linear dynamics. By means of the observer, the distributed control law of each agent is designed using local information to guarantee consensus, and the corresponding sufficient conditions are obtained by exploiting graph and control theory approach. A modified distributed event-triggered consensus protocol is designed to reduce communication congestion. Detailed analysis of the leaderless and the leader-following consensus is presented for both observer-based and full-information protocols. Finally, two simulation examples are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and capabilities of the established theories.

hits.text: To address the challenges faced by virtual power plants (VPPs) in uncertain market environments and complex distribution networks, including strong market coupling, difficulty in multi-resource coordination, and strict safety constraints, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Hybrid Intelligent Framework (H2IF).
